articles.title: FBI Using AI To Stop School Shootings; Doomers Want It Paused
articles.description: FBI Using AI To Stop School Shootings; Doomers Want It Paused Authored by Steve Watson via Modernity News , While the same 'current thing' leftists who spent years on climate, oil and "Palestine" now chants that AI will wipe out the human race, FBI Director Kash Patel just announced that the agency is using the technology to actively prevent mass shootings, including school attacks, before they happen. Patel said artificial intelligence helped the bureau prevent possible school shootings in North Carolina and about half a dozen other states, and that he has increased the FBI's use of AI by 605 percent. That is the version of AI that the pause-and-treaty crowd does not want discussed. ? JUST NOW: In a MASSIVE win, FBI Director Kash Patel announces that half-a-dozen states' possible school SH00TINGS were thwarted through the use of AI One was just stopped in North Carolina ?? "We've done it in North Carolina and about half-a-dozen other states to prevent... pic.twitter.com/SKzwJIkvnV — Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) September 19, 2026 The comments match what he told the Senate Judiciary Committee days earlier. When he took the job, the bureau had two test use cases for artificial intelligence. "We just hit our 140th, that's a 605 percent increase since I've been in this seat, to process information to triage intelligence, analyze, and get this information out to our local partners." This is not a science-fiction sermon. It is tip triage. Patel has been making the operational case since spring. On Sean Hannity's podcast he said the old FBI treated modernization as an afterthought. "AI was never used at the FBI till we got there, literally crazy," he said. "I'm using it everywhere." The bottleneck was volume. The National Threat Operations Center takes thousands of tips a week. "If we had just humans look at it, we would never sift through them all." He put the question more sharply still: "What's the point of collecting terabytes of data if you can't sift through it?" The North Carolina case is the one he keeps returning to. "We stopped a school massacre in North Carolina because we got a tip and we were able to triage it with artificial intelligence." A separate New York school threat, he said, was disrupted after "a tip from our private-sector partners who are building out AI infrastructure." In a Fox News op-ed he described the machinery. When a call hits NTOC, AI generates a transcript, drafts a summary of the threat, scans open cases for matches, and assigns a lead value so the hottest tips rise first. "This specific threat intake process helped the FBI quickly act and stop an attacker plotting a mass shooting at a North Carolina preschool," Patel urged. The same overhaul, he wrote, helped the bureau identify and locate 6,300 missing children last year - a 30 percent increase - and arrest 2,000 abusers, a 20 percent increase. In a Richmond case, facial recognition tools were used to pull 8- and 12-year-old children away from a would-be abuser now facing 50 years. The tools are being used to rank leads and get them to agents and local partners before someone walks through a school door. It's not something that has been considered by the doomer leftists now literally calling for AI to be 'switched off'. San Francisco and London just got an NPC software update. The banners changed. The wardrobe did not. Dozens marched from OpenAI's Mission Bay headquarters to Anthropic's offices and on to San Francisco City Hall, demanding Mayor Daniel Lurie declare a local "AI state of emergency." Chalk on the pavement read "Extinction is on the table." Organiser Hunter Glenn told reporters, "I was pretty scared about the possibility of extinction for awhile." In London, "PauseAI" and "Pull The Plug" rallies formed after Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger said he personally believed there was a greater than 10 percent chance AI could "kill all humans" within a decade. Their slogan: "10% chance of extinction? 100% chance of resistance." Scott Jennings had already mapped the rotation. "It's always the same apocalyptic crowd moving from one issue to the next. Responsible guardrails are one thing, but handicapping American innovation while China speeds ahead with zero regulation isn't sound policy - it's just foolish." Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gave the extinction industry a simpler number. There is a "0% chance" the world ends in 2030. "2030 is not going to be the end of the world." A U.S. pause would not freeze the technology. It would freeze the labs already winning and hand the century's defining stack to Beijing. Europe sold GDPR as virtue and now hosts none of the world's dominant labs. Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale told Jesse Watters the scare is not civic caution. It is a campaign. "These guys don't believe in God. They're atheists, but they've created something they believe is God," Watters said, laying out Lonsdale's point. "This is their Messiah, and this is their end of the world." Lonsdale was direct. "There is a coordinated campaign to make the American people afraid." San Francisco, he said, dropped Christianity and still wanted a messiah and an apocalypse. "If you give up religion, you want some kind of messianic complex, some kind of big thing to believe in. These effective altruists - this is their Messiah, this is their end of the world, this is their obsession." An industrial revolution is coming that would be "amazing for America if we get it right." The people trying to stop it, Lonsdale said, "hate America." That theology now has a policy shop. Bill Gates is back on the emergency circuit calling AI an "alien intelligence." "I don't think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be," he told Reuters. "Governments are way behind on this one." Then the Hollywood script: "There's all sorts of movies where some aliens are coming, and magically the US and China and everybody comes together to solve the problem. AI is kind of like this alien intelligence. It's here, and we better do like it shows in those movies." On a podcast he went further. "It's not the role of the industry to self-regulate or understand the whole-of-society impact that comes out of AI." He wants a permanent cross-border watchdog stitched from nuclear inspections, aviation rules and ozone treaties - and a meeting with Xi Jinping. In the same news cycle his foundation pledged $1 billion over two years to spread AI through schools, clinics and farms. Alarm in one hand. Pipeline in the other. President Trump has already rejected the slowdown. "We're leading China in AI," he said. "Whoever wins AI, wins." A lot of the horror stories being shopped around, he added, "won't happen." Trump also answered the doomer circuit with an appointment, not a pause. He said he is forming an "AI Force," modeled on Space Force, and will name a high-IQ "AI Czar" to keep the United States first while the left's latest scare campaign is treated as what he called it: another hoax. "AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country's GDP," he said. "We are leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way." "We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows," Trump added, noting that bad actors can be handled with the criminal and civil courts already on the books - not a Gates-style global leash. ? BREAKING: President Trump announces he will be appointing a HIGH IQ "AI CZAR" and launches the "AI FORCE" Trump says we will UNLEASH AI and that the propaganda will fail All of this will be geared towards not only BUSTING anti-AI hoaxes but keeping America number one. LET'S... pic.twitter.com/Cy3T8R1cBK — Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) September 19, 2026 One future is the FBI using models to transcribe a threat call, score it, match it, and get a cop to a North Carolina preschool before the shooting starts. The other is a global committee, a Netflix doom documentary sold as the new Inconvenient Truth , and a street mob that needs the next wipeout the way some people need a weather report. China is not holding a pause-and-pray summit. Chinese firms have been accused by U.S. officials of stripping American models at industrial scale. Beijing's spy chief has treated AI as a Party-control problem, which is another way of saying the CCP wants the weapon. Patel's point is narrower and harder to slogan away. Used by cops, under the law, the same class of tools the doomers want parked under an international inspectorate is already being used to find missing kids, rank tips, and stop school plots. Every plot that never makes a headline is a child who goes home. America can build the thing, police the abuse, and keep the lead. Or it can let the extinction church write the rules while the bureau that just started using the tools is told to wait for permission from a committee Gates wants to staff. articles.title: EIT Community Hub Malta encourages Maltese innovators to connect with European innovation networks
articles.description: EIT Community Hub Malta, which is supported by the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), a body of the European Union is encouraging Maltese businesses, start-ups, universities, researchers and other organisations with ambitions to grow internationally to tap into EIT's extensive innovation network. This network has been specifically designed strengthen Europe's innovation capacity. The EIT Community Hub Malta is highlighting the opportunities available through the EIT's Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs), which bring together companies, SMEs and start-ups, universities, research organisations, investors, public bodies and civil society organisations from across Europe. For Maltese organisations, becoming involved in these communities can provide access to potential commercial and research partners, specialist expertise, consortium building and matchmaking opportunities, innovation programmes, training and greater visibility within European innovation ecosystems. Diana Miceli, EIT Community Officer Malta, said, "For Maltese organisations serious about growing internationally, we need to think beyond individual funding calls. A European strategy is also a relationship strategy. The EIT communities bring together the right companies, universities, researchers and innovators that Maltese organisations may want to work with when addressing a societal challenge. Rather than approaching every European opportunity from scratch, becoming part of these networks can help Maltese organisations build relationships and establish a stronger presence within the ecosystems where new collaborations and projects are being developed." The EIT's communities span a broad range of sectors that are directly relevant to Malta's economy and research community. These include climate innovation and resilience; digital technologies, deep tech, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity; food and agriculture; healthcare and life sciences; sustainable energy; raw materials and the circular economy; water resilience and the blue economy; cultural and creative industries and sustainable transport and urban mobility. While access to funding is an important part of the European innovation landscape, participation in these networks can offer benefits well before a funding application is submitted. European research and innovation projects frequently depend on strong international consortia, while commercial expansion and technology development can require relationships with businesses, researchers, customers and specialist partners outside Malta. Different EIT communities offer different membership, partnership and engagement models, with the appropriate route depending on the organisation's sector, size, objectives and level of involvement. Membership or partnership fees may apply in some cases and participation does not guarantee access to funding or selection for projects. Instead, its value lies in giving organisations the opportunity to become active participants in networks where partnerships, projects and commercial opportunities are continually being developed. Miceli said organisations should therefore consider their longer-term European ambitions when deciding whether participation in an EIT community could be beneficial. "The starting point should be where an organisation wants to be in Europe in three to five years, which organisations it needs to know and which networks can help it build those relationships. Malta's size should not prevent our businesses, researchers and innovators from being part of Europe's largest innovation ecosystems." The EIT Community Hub Malta can help local organisations identify the communities most relevant to their activities and ambitions and explore the membership, partnership and other engagement opportunities available. Organisations interested in finding out which EIT community could be the right fit for them can contact Diana Miceli, EIT Community Officer Malta, at malta@eitcommunity.eu for an initial discussion about the opportunities available and the most appropriate route into the EIT Community. articles.title: Barclays sees BSP hiking rates in October as oil, record-low peso fan inflation risks
articles.description: British banking giant Barclays expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to again hike interest rates next month as high oil prices and a record-low peso threaten to intensify inflationary pressures while worsening the Philippines’ trade balance. In a report last Friday, Sept. 18, Barclays Bank said it now sees the BSP further tightening monetary policy after raising the policy rate by 25 basis points (bps) to five percent last August. “The recent resurgence in global crude oil prices—even if they appear to have peaked at the time of writing—coupled with recent Philippine peso depreciation will likely unnerve the BSP into delivering one more 25-bp rate hike, to 5.25 percent, than we earlier expected, in October 2026, though we view this as a relatively close call,” Barclays said. If Barclays’ forecast is realized, the upcoming October hike would be the BSP’s fourth straight 25-bp increase since April, bringing cumulative tightening to 100 bps. The peso’s depreciation has added to inflation concerns, with the local currency sinking to a new historic-low close of ₱62.86 against the United States (US) dollar last week amid elevated global oil prices caused by the prolonged war between the US and Iran. Barclays nonetheless expects the BSP to begin cutting interest rates in June next year, eventually bringing the policy rate back down to 4.25 percent. Barclays ’ monetary policy outlook comes as the Philippines emerges as one of the economies in the region whose external trade position has been more visibly hurt by the war in the Middle East. The report said emerging Asian economies have generally been able to secure the oil and gas they need despite disruptions, although they are paying considerably more for their energy imports. While the jump in the value of oil and gas imports was expected, Barclays noted that not all net energy importers in the region suffered a deterioration in their merchandise trade balances. Major semiconductor exporters, in particular, benefited from strong artificial intelligence (AI)-related exports that likely helped pay for higher energy imports from a current account perspective. However, the Philippines has not enjoyed the same degree of protection. Barclays said the Philippines and Thailand “experienced a clearer erosion of their merchandise trade balances since the Middle East conflict broke out.” Despite these external pressures, Barclays kept its Philippine economic growth forecasts unchanged at three percent for 2026 and five percent for 2027. Its projection for this year falls below the government’s downgraded 3.5- to 4.5-percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth target, while its forecast for next year is at the bottom end of the also downscaled five- to six-percent goal. GDP grew by a post-pandemic low of 2.3 percent in the second quarter of 2026, with Barclays projecting growth to improve slightly to 3.2 percent in the third quarter, before accelerating to 5.7 percent in the fourth quarter. Barclays also slightly lowered its Philippine inflation forecast for 2026 to 5.6 percent from 5.7 percent previously. This would still put full-year inflation well above the BSP’s two- to four-percent target range amid the continued impact of higher energy costs. For 2027, Barclays expects headline inflation to ease to 3.8 percent, bringing the annual rate back within the BSP’s target band.

articles.title: DigiPlus looks outside Asia as overseas gaming revenue begins to trickle in
articles.description: DigiPlus Interactive Corp. has begun generating revenue from its newly launched gaming operations in Brazil as it continues scanning for opportunities outside Asia. Speaking on the sidelines of the Inside Asian Gaming EXPO, DigiPlus Chief Global Growth Officer Erick Su noted that tweaks made to the platform have driven stronger revenue performance compared to its initial soft launch. The platform ran for roughly three weeks starting in September 2024 before DigiPlus took a strategic pause on October 10, 2024, to retool the system for better alignment with Brazilian preferences. “I think it’s going okay. We improved the revenue we have, and you probably can see some of the reports in the third quarter when we have a financial release,” Su said. However, he admitted that figures remain modest relative to their core market. “Obviously, it’s still relatively low compared to what we have in the Philippines... We are still progressing to see if we can expand the business [and] increase revenue... So, our international market is still in the exploration stage,” Su said. Su also noted headwinds in Latin America. Beyond high market competition, he pointed to broader policy instability: “Recently, there’s a lot of turbulence about policy, and the President talked about banning online gambling.” Meanwhile, DigiPlus has 10 months remaining on its one-year timeline to launch in South Africa following its license approval. “For South Africa, we need to start a new market at this time. So, we are probably going to be working with some third-party partners and see what we can do there,” Su explained. The company is currently mapping out global strategy to identify regions that best match its capabilities. “We want to launch somewhere that recognizes us well... That would be outside Asia... Since we are only targeting legalized markets, in Asia there is a very limited choice. Only the Philippines, Australia, and newly legalized New Zealand fit,” he noted. He added that other key hubs offer little entry: “Markets like Hong Kong and Singapore are monopolies, so at the moment, there are no other options in Asia.” To navigate these hurdles, DigiPlus is engaging external advisors versed in local regulatory frameworks. “We try to continue to explore the opportunity.” The company is also pursuing expansion in New Zealand after its board approved the filing of an Expression of Interest for an operating license.
